 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 (for short,
hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act') against the judgment and award dated 02.11.2021 passed in MVC No.652/2020 by the MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-11) for enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for appellant and learned counsel for respondents.
3. The status of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.
4. The case of the petitioner is that he has filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
On 01.12.2019 at 4.30 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Bike as a pillion rider, at that time, a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-42-N-2372 came from Magadi side and dashed to the motorcycle.
Due to which, he has sustained fracture injures on his right leg and was treated as an in-patient and spent lot of amount towards medical expenses and he has suffering from disability.
Hence claims compensation under various heads.

5. The respondent No.2 - Insurer has filed statement of objections denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car and other averments made in the claim petition as false and prays for dismissing the claim petition and the owner of the offending vehicle has been placed as an exparte.

6. Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 01.12.2019 at about 4.30 a.m., near Gungarahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli,
Ramanagara Taluk, while he was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-42-EA-0384 as a pillion rider, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-42-N- 2372 by its driver?

2 NC: 2024:KHC:27648 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
7. The claimant to prove his case, examined himself as P.W.1 and examined Doctor as P.W.2 and got marked 14 documents as Exs.P.1 to P.14.
The respondents have not examined any witnesses or produced any documents.
8. Accordingly, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.4,16,000/-.
The same is challenged by the claimant for enhancement of compensation.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner is working as a Driver and he was relieved from the service as per Ex.P.11 and he was earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month and the same was not properly considered by the Tribunal.
The compensation awarded all the heads is very meager and needs to be interfered with.
Hence, prays for enhancing the same.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 objects the same and supported the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and prays for dismissing appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments and on perusing the records, the point that arises for my consideration is as under:-
Whether the appellant is entitled for the enhanced compensation?
If so, to what extent?

12. On perusal of the record, the accident in question dated 01.12.2019 occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car by its Driver is not in dispute, only the quantum of compensation is challenged by the claimant in this case.
The petitioner has sustained right leg proximal tibia fracture.
He was admitted in the hospital for 6 days and later, he has taken further treatment as out-patient.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and the same is just and proper and needs no interference.
Towards medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.94,000/- based on the actual bills produced and hence, the same is kept intact.

14. Towards 'food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges', a sum of Rs.2,400/- is awarded and a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head 'conveyance' by the Tribunal is Sri Mutharaju vs Sri Hanumanthe Gowda on 15 July, 2024

and considering the nature of injuries, I propose to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the said head.
15. Towards loss of income during laid up period, the Tribunal has considered income at Rs.14,000/- per month as per the chart of the KSLSA.
In the present case, the petitioner is a Driver and he has been relieved from the job as per the letter issued by the school authorities at Ex.P.11.
In the said letter, it mentioned that the petitioner was a Driver and immediately, after the accident he has been relieved from his job.
Therefore considering income of the petitioner at Rs.14,000/- is not correct and hence, I propose to consider Rs.15,000/- per month as income of the petitioner.

Considering the nature of NC: 2024:KHC:27648 injuries, the petitioner might have taken bed rest for three months and hence, an amount of Rs.45,000/- (15,000 x 3) is awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.

16. Towards 'loss of amenities', the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- where the petitioner was aged about 36 years at the time of the accident and he has to suffer for long period due to his disability.

Hence I propose to award 25,000/- towards the 'loss of amenities'.
17.

Towards 'loss of income due to disability', considering the income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month and the Doctor has assessed 38% disability to the right lower limb and 13%
to the whole body.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly taken the 13% of disability.
As the petitioner is aged about 36 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '15'.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.3,51,000/- (15,000 x 12 x 15 x 13%) is awarded under the head 'loss of income due to disability'.
18. As regard to the future medical expenses, there is a still implants fixed inside the leg and petitioner needs NC: 2024:KHC:27648 another surgery for removal of implants.

The Tribunal has rightly awarded an amount of Rs.20,000/-, which is meager considering the fact that implants to be removed, I propose to award an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards 'future medical expenses'.

19. Accordingly, appellant entitled for compensation as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Towards injury pain and 50,000-00 suffering Towards medical expenses.
94,000-00 Towards food and extra 15,000-00 nourishment and medical attendant and conveyance Towards loss of income 45,000-00
during treatment Towards loss of future 3,51,000-00 earning capacity Deprivation of future 25,000-00 amenities Deprivation of future 50,000-00 medical expenses

awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation.
Interest is excluding the future medical expenses.
2. 60 days is granted for depositing the award amount apportionment made by the Tribunal.
